chapter: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
title: Arnheim's band in Minneapolis and New York with Jimmy Mundy
summary: Budd drives to Minneapolis and then the Hotel New Yorker, writes four arrangements weekly, and Arnheim backs his authority as musical director.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: All right. So, I'm with -- I take my wife with me. I bought a car. I went to Minneapolis and we worked at the Nicolette Hotel. And, while I was up there, I bought me an Oldsmobile sport coupe. Second hand. But, it was big. And, Gus Arnheim, he stood for the thing so I could travel with it. And, when we left Minneapolis, I stopped through Chicago and picked up my wife, and then we came to New York.
We came to New York and worked at the Hotel New Yorker for the ice show.

This was '37. All in '37. So, I'm making four arrangements a week and copying them. For the band. Myself. I couldn't (inaudible). I was trying to make all of that money. I didn't want to give the money -- and, Jimmy Munday was also here writing for Benny Goodman at the time, and I -- I got a room right across the street from Jimmy Munday, and I was staying up on the 135th right off of Seventh Avenue, and Munday was staying across the street downstairs. He had like an English basement apartment.

And, so, we would go down and write together and talk and everything, and I would be doing my work, he would be doing his work. So, I took -- the first rehearsal we had in New York, I had my four arrangements and I took them down. So, Gus Arnheim says, "Just a minute, Budd, before you rehearse the band." Now, he said, "Gentlemen, I want you to know this now. Budd Johnson, as you know, is the musical director. He's the arranger for the band. And, if he tells me anybody can't play his music, then you better look for another job."

He say, "So, I just want that understood, so you better pay close attention to him and see what he's got to tell you, you know." He gave me that respect. Well, of course, I mean, I never had no problem with the guys. You know what I mean. Because, I'm hanging out with them and having a ball. Joe Dixon was in that band at the time.
